claims.statement: The guidance recommends an ACCESSIBILITY.md to make accessibility information discoverable and provide a barrier-reporting route; a file does not prove accessibility conformance.
The published body says GitHub displays an Accessibility overview tab and About link when the repository contains ACCESSIBILITY.md; actual UI behavior is not observed by this review.
The documented local-file precedence is .github directory first, repository root second, docs directory third.
If a repository lacks a local accessibility page, it can inherit one from an organization-owned .github repository; inherited content must be resolved rather than silently treated as local absence.

Suggested content dimensions are priorities, supported environments, known barriers, contributor expectations, reporting, ownership and maintenance; these suggestions are not mandatory adopted controls.
The Community Standards template path is described for public repositories; no equivalent private-repository template capability is inferred.
The template procedure uses repository Insights, Community Standards and Add/Propose for Accessibility; described navigation does not verify the current actor's permissions.
Template instructions should be replaced with project-specific accessibility information; instructions stored in comments do not appear in rendered output.
The template workflow requests a meaningful commit message and permits multi-author attribution; linked attribution instructions are not transitively reviewed.
When starting on the default branch, the guidance recommends a new branch and pull request rather than a direct default-branch commit; no branch protection is inferred.
Commit/Propose controls submit the proposed change; this evidence review does not perform that action.
The manual procedure uses Add file/Create new file or the file-tree plus control; UI icons and image alt text were read, not independently rendered-image reviewed.
The manual procedure permits ACCESSIBILITY.md in the root, .github or docs, then editing accessibility-related information; file existence alone does not validate content quality.
The manual commit workflow repeats a meaningful message and optional multi-author attribution; documentation is not an actual commit receipt.
The author-email dropdown is described as showing only verified addresses; with email privacy enabled, no-reply is the default, not a guarantee that every publication preserves privacy.
The manual default-branch workflow also recommends a new branch and pull request before Commit/Propose; no publishing permission is granted by imported guidance.

review_scope: Complete63-line acquired body read. File precedence, organizational fallback, template/public scope, comment visibility, manual creation, commit/branch and email-privacy workflow retained. Independently authored reference claims only; imported examples/instructions not executed.
version_differences: Links are version-qualified in the Enterprise Cloud body. Separate body-specific digests and spans prevent collapsing versions into byte-identical evidence.
remaining: Linked commit/PR/email guidance and image rights review
